extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy and classical education; educators and theorists considering ideal curricula for rulers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating the Platonic curriculum, selection, and character requirements for the guardian/ruler class in an ideal state, including the order of studies and moral dispositions required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator's intention: common happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislator did not aim at making any one class in the State happy above the rest; the happiness was to be in the whole State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and education should bind citizens to be benefactors of the State and of one another; institutions are justified by the common good, not private pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians as benefactors obliged to public service
rubrics_metrics.description: Compel philosophers/guardians to have a care and providence of others; they shall be benefactors of the State and therefore benefactors of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain to guardians that, unlike in other states, they are obliged to share in political toils; selection and social framing must make public service a duty, not optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers should be reluctant to govern
rubrics_metrics.description: The State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed; the State in which they are most eager is the worst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer rulers who accept office as stern necessity rather than seekers of power; avoid incentivising ambition for office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must possess a better life (virtue over wealth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrive for future rulers another and a better life than that of a ruler; they must be rich not in silver and gold, but in virtue and wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create honors and alternative rewards that make philosophy and virtue the chief goods, preventing pursuit of private advantage and office-grabbing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid lovers of political task among governors
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who govern ought not to be lovers of the task; if they are, there will be rival lovers and they will fight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and education should eliminate disposition that relishes political competition; encourage sense of duty and reluctance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be both warriors and philosophers
rubrics_metrics.description: Our guardian is both warrior and philosopher; the same persons must be capable of military usefulness and of rising to contemplation of being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum and training should combine physical/gymnastic and martial instruction with rigorous intellectual formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics (arithmetic) as liberating study
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and calculation draw the soul from becoming to being; arithmetic compels the soul to reason about abstract number and leads the mind towards truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach arithmetic not as a commercial tool but to develop abstract thought and the soul's capacity to contemplate universals; arithmetic is both militarily useful and philosophically formative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry for apprehending eternal truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometry aims at knowledge of the eternal, not of aught perishing and transient; it compels the soul to view being and creates the spirit of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include rigorous geometry in education; emphasise its role in turning the mind to immutable forms rather than merely practical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomy ordered for higher apprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Astronomy should be used to apprehend true motions by reason, as patterns pointing beyond the visible, not to investigate material particulars as if eternal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach astronomy as a vehicle for reasoning about true number and figure; avoid treating celestial observation as an end in itself or conflating visible regularities with eternal truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonics/music with philosophical aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and harmony should not be pursued merely in practice; teachers who study only audible harmonies err unless they connect the science with the beautiful and good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use studies of harmony to cultivate the soul's order and taste, but only insofar as they lead toward the higher object (the good); avoid narrow technicalism of Pythagoreans or mere technicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studies must intercommunicate and connect
rubrics_metrics.description: When all these studies reach the point of inter-communion and connection with one another, and come to be considered in their mutual affinities, then the pursuit of them will have value; otherwise there is no profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curriculum so disciplines support and lead into one another (arithmetics → geometry → astronomy → harmonics → dialectic), forming a coherent educational ascent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectic as the supreme science
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic is the coping-stone of the sciences; it alone goes directly to the first principle and is the only science which does away with hypotheses to make her ground secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat dialectic as culminating study that enables direct apprehension of the idea of the good; it must be taught to move students from opinion to pure intellect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite study before dialectic
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic alone can reveal the absolute; but only to one who is a disciple of the previous sciences—the mathematical and other preparatory studies are handmaids to dialectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require mastery of earlier mathematical and related disciplines before engaging in dialectic; these serve as necessary preparation rather than ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim educationally to move soul from becoming to being
rubrics_metrics.description: The education must enable the soul to pass from becoming (change, sensory world) to being (true, eternal reality), culminating in perception of the absolute good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure studies and exercises to shift attention from sensory particulars to abstraction and first principles; evaluate success by the student's capacity for dialectical abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection: natural gifts and dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose rulers with keenness and ready powers of acquisition, good memory, unwearied industry, sound body and mind, and a love of labour in study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference given to the surest, bravest, and, if possible, the fairest; select those whose natural temperaments facilitate sustained intellectual discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish true sons of philosophy from bastards
rubrics_metrics.description: True votaries of philosophy should not be half-industrious or halting; avoid those who prefer gymnastic and hunting to labour of learning, or who are patient of involuntary falsehood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess candidates for wholehearted devotion to intellectual labour and moral seriousness; treat habitually lax or one-sided temperaments as disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral virtues must be integrated (temperance, courage, magnificence)
rubrics_metrics.description: In respect of temperance, courage, magnificence, and every other virtue, carefully distinguish between the true son and the bastard; defects in any part of virtue make one unfit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prospective rulers for full, balanced virtue rather than partial excellence; moral defects undermine fitness to rule and harm the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational outcome: skill in dialectical questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a law that they shall have such an education as will enable them to attain the greatest skill in asking and answering questions—training in dialectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readiness by capacity to abstract, define ideas (including the idea of the good), endure objections, and respond by appeal to absolute truth rather than opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude toward study: philosophical, not mercantile
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must pursue studies not as merchants or retail-traders with a view to buying and selling, but in the spirit of a philosopher for the sake of the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage instrumental, profit-driven approaches to learning; encourage disinterested inquiry and reverence for truth as an educational norm.
